Concept seems interesting, but the gameplay is really dull. 1. There is a progression of sorts, but it's incredibly limited and very very grindy. The grid sees you lose again and again, and losing is not fun 2. The space you have to work with is very small, as a result you build pretty much the same way every time. After 2-3 games you just feel like going through the motions 3. Enemy variety is very limited, and there is no variation at all, you always get same exact enemies at same exact times in same exact amounts. 4. Game pace is bad. Overall it's very slow, you gain resources painfully slowly, and you're just waiting and "hand"-minding half the time. Other times, you have a wave to deal with, and would like some time to think, but there is no pause, so you're rushed for no apparent reason. 5. When I say concepts are interesting, I mean that it's like factorio. But actually worse. Factorio had space, here you don't have space, it would imply that this game is more of a puzzle where you have to pack your base really well, but that aspect is no utilized at all. So overall - there's nothing new here, it could be good, but it's not. Overall, feels like a decent tech demo, but a very poor "game".

Fun and addictive game with a fresh take on tower defense! Build a factory to gather resources, expand your base, and construct powerful towers. You can use a tactical pause to plan your next move. Each level features a unique boss, and defeating it grants you a useful reward. You can also finish a level early by destroying the enemy tower. Between levels, there’s a tech tree that you can upgrade to improve your abilities. At the time of writing (v0.3.4), the game includes three modes and four levels: Classic: Standard difficulty; you cannot build during tactical pause. Strategy: Similar to Classic, but you can build during tactical pause. Hardcore: Play previously completed maps, but enemies are stronger and tactical pause is disabled. Each level feels distinct, although levels 1 and 2 share a similar layout, as do levels 3 and 4. However, the strategy you need changes. For example, in level 3, the trees have fewer resources but are grouped closely together, while in level 4, the same trees are spread farther apart (but still close together).

It is a terrible idea to mix tower defence and factory building. The time pressure demands on the two species of game are entirely incompatible. Despite this, this game has extremely good art, and is likely to never have a competitor that offers comparable gameplay.

实际上你要做的就是满地挖矿，并在挖完之后把产线原封不动的搬迁到新矿上 但如果仅此而已我最多给中评或者懒得写评价，这游戏要命的是，没有框选-复制-粘贴，也没有蓝图功能。 纯手动重复完全一样的工作，我玩着最直接的感受就是坐牢。 其实即便有了蓝图我也相当怀疑这游戏结合拉产线和塔防推关的玩法到底有没有前途，传送带拉产线自动化按理说应该绑定的爽点是那种从基础生产到产能逐渐扩大升级，逐步堆砌打造精密复杂大型物流系统(屎山)的快感。而这游戏关卡模式是限时波次boss，所有建造的东西通关就清除，我很难玩得爽 Essentially, all you have to do is mine everywhere and then relocate your production line to the new mine spot, intact. But if that were all, I'd give it a mediocre review or not bother writing a review at most. The frustrating thing about this game is the lack of a selection-copy-paste function or a blueprint feature. Manually repeating the same tasks made me feel like an Orc Peon. Even with blueprints, I seriously doubt the future of this game's combination of production line automation and tower defense gameplay. The automated production line system should ideally be about the satisfaction of gradually expanding and upgrading from basic production to a complex logistics system (or tons of spaghetti code but somehow running fine). However, this game's level mode features timed wave bosses, and everything you build is wiped out upon completion, making it difficult for me to enjoy building. I'm not sure if having an endless mode or something similar would be better.

This is not your typical Tower Defense game where you can sit back and relax while watching your towers shoot at waves of incoming enemies, this game is the opposite of that where you will be constantly doing something from the moment you start a level, and that's what makes it so good. It will probably feel like you're playing Starcraft with how quickly you'll need to be managing your resources, setting up defenses, and exploring the area. It can become pretty challenging in the later levels, even more so if you're playing on expert mode, but also very satisfying when you finally manage to beat a level or one of the bosses. Highly recommended if you're looking for something a little different than the normal Tower Defense experience.

I like the game, the graphics, the resource gathering, the tower defense aspect. The game breaker, in my view, is the fact that to progress and win the game you have to make fire towers to break the fog of war to find crystals and the enemy castle to use the crystals on. There is no indication where these things are you have to guess, which puts it into a luck situation. It doesn't matter how much planning you do. One of the resources needed to make the fire tower comes from defeating enemies and the longer the game goes the more there are. If you head in the wrong direction with fire towers you lose the game because the number of enemies will get overwhelming before you can find what you're looking for. It makes no sense to have the game hinge on luck instead of stategy.

As of writing this review, Tower Factory is still in early access, and it is a solo-dev project, so if you can live with all that entails, it's worth the current price of 15 bucks. It took me about 30 hours to beat all the levels...though some of them I had to play a few times. There are only 6 levels so far, but more are planned. A tower defense game that is also a factory-builder is a fun twist on both genres. It reminds me a lot of Diplomacy is not an option, in that the simple, low-poly design makes you think it will be pretty casual, then WHAM! a surprisingly difficult game. But there are multiple difficulty settings, so you can find an option that will be challenging, but doable for you, no matter your skill level.
Good game to kill time and switch off from real life, where You have to work on planning and resource management. I personally recommend it.

This is one of the more unique game concepts that I have played. It combines a factory sim game and a traditional tower defense game with exploration, rogue-like, and strategy elements. The difficultly scaling feels super nice with levels increasing in difficulty and complexity as you learn how to best build a factory that can support the towers you need to survive. If you're a fan of games like Satisfactory, Factorio, Bloons Tower Defense, and base building games, I think you would enjoy this game!

I normally dont buy early access games anymore because of their reputation, but i saw the developer of Tower Factory using their real name publicly and knew this had to be something special. Not just a throw away company with no traceable reputation that disapears after money is made, but instead a real person with a face and name. And was I right to trust this little game. I thought there were hardly any good tower defence games being made anymore, and then Tower Factory turned that notion on its head and blew me away. [b]Gameplay;[/b] The main gameplay revolves around 3 main elements: Exploration, Resource Production and Tower Defence. [u]Exploration[/u] is done by using fog of war, you have a starting area where you can see and build and have to place beacons to extend your vision. Terrain you explore has resources you need to build and upgrade towers and expand your factory, but you will also reveal resource chests and coin chests (meta progession) that help you as you explore futher. Lastly there are crystals that you have to find that allows you to create a win condition. Because exploration is not just a means to an end, but actively rewards you with each step towards winning a round... it feels like a game mechanic properly done and fun to do. [u]Resource Production[/u] is done in a similar way as Factorio, you place down resource collectors and build transport belts to get them where you need them. These resources can then be made into other more refined resources or used as is, meaning the factory gets more complicated as you build and upgrade more complicated towers. This does not get tedious because the resources variety is limited, and production buildings have 2 recipes that you can swap between. Making the process smooth and easier to control than games that focus purely on factory building and management. Need more planks? just put a sawmill on the belt that has wood logs. Stakes? swap the sawmill recipe till you have what you need. [u]Tower Defence[/u] is done in a way that is not too easy mainly due to meta progression. You start with 3 tower types and can upgrade them once, but can research more tower types and a special upgrade as you play more. Towers can only be upgraded if they shoot the enemy and gain experience, and require resources to do so. As you play more you will collect coins that you can spend on a research tree, that lets you buy tower upgrades that give slow or DoT damage. [b]Win Conditions[/b] are done in an interesting but fair way. The first win condition is collecting 3 crystals that are scattered around the map. Exploration using becons to reveal more of the map is key, and there are always more crystals than you need. Once you have 3 or more crystals, you have to find the enemy castle and can destroy it at any time winning the round. The second win condition is defeating the boss. This is done by surviving all waves and waiting for the boss to come out at the last wave. This is no easy feat and cant be done with the starting towers without upgrades. This allows for replayability as you get closer to defeating bosses. Even when you aim to kill the boss you have the option to win the round at any time by destroying the castle with 3 crystals. So it never feels unfair even if you are not far enough in the research and upgrade tree to deal with a boss. [b]Map, Progression, Replayability;[/b] The map is randomly generated, spawning in resources, tower upgrade patches, chests and crystals. This means even if you select the same map, the only thing thats the same each time you play is the boss of that map. Progression is done by a research tree where you spend coins. You get coins from losing or winning a map, and can collect more coins by exploring the map and finding chests. Upgrades make the game easier and opens more ways to play. Not just tower upgrades and unlocks but also starting resources, castle hitpoints and sight radius. How hard the game is, is something you have some control over. The game has multiple gamemodes, multiple maps, an extensive research/upgrade tree, so plenty of replayability even in early access. [b]Early Access;[/b] I have yet to give feedback/suggestions, or followed the community doing so. So I cant comment on the EA progress, and what the developer(s) do with the feedback yet. I will update this section when I have better insight on the EA process. [b]The Medicore and Bad;[/b] Currently some maps are much harder than others due to the starting resources being sparse or further away from the starting area. Its fully playable every map i played, but starting resources can set you back quite a bit. This could be a bit better balanced. I have not found any bugs or other issues with the game. [b]Verdict;[/b] If you like tower defence games this game is worth picking up. When you also enjoy base building and automation, this game becomes a must buy. The full price of 15 euros is fair and the game does not need a (big) discount to be worth the price.

This game scratched the exact itch I was looking for, as someone who loves both factory building and tower defense games. I really appreciate the existence of Strategic Mode, which lets you build while paused, since it allows for a more relaxing and satisfying (in my opinion) playthrough of the main campaign. Then once I felt like I understood the mechanics well, I switched to hard difficulty to play in Endless mode. [h3]You will probably love this game if you:[/h3] - enjoy the early-game stage of factory building games like Satisfactory and Factorio - always wished your tower defense games had more of an economy to them - like chopping trees and destroying rocks, and clearing out a nice area to build in - wish making a factory could be not just a strategy to plan out, but a skill to master, as you learn to slap down a production line in seconds - have it out for mushrooms and snowmen, and like big lasers [h3]You might not enjoy this game as much if you:[/h3] - need your factories to stick around longer than a few hours - prefer to plot out complex production chains rather than mastering simple, quick to build ones - get frustrated by resource nodes that run out - have a phobia of procedural generation & roguelike mechanics The game is still in development as I write this review, so I'm excited to see what new map mechanics, towers, resources, and production opportunities appear with Tier 3!
